title: Runs orphaned by a dead supervisor sit in 'stopping' forever and clutter tk cloud status
description:
Data hygiene left behind by tick 2xm's defect, not by 2xm's fix.

Before 2xm, every cloud run's supervising Workflow errored at Cloudflare's 10-minute step cap. Only the Workflow writes the run's state column, so a run whose Workflow is gone can never leave a non-terminal state. Four such rows remain:

  run_9e40b9563bfb493cac1fe6625356e538  stopping
  run_2e66e765f74c4192b2b9a24a6e8415cf  stopping
  run_f15efdfb79a84bda9914e92a39395f3d  stopping
  run_0573d3c74ab84d6abc1ac1a539c9933a  failed

They hold nothing — the lease moved on correctly each time and no containers survive — so this is clutter rather than a hazard. It is filed because 'tk cloud status' is the operator's first view of the factory, and four permanently-stuck rows train the reader to ignore the state column, which is the column that matters when something is genuinely wrong.

Runs after 2xm reach terminal states correctly (run_b42d0eb6 reached 'stopped' with workflow 'complete'), so this is a backlog to drain, not an ongoing leak.

Two things worth doing, and the second is the durable one:
1. Drain the existing rows — a one-off admin path, or a reaper that transitions a run whose Workflow instance is absent or errored.
2. The general rule: a run's state should be derivable from evidence outside the writer that may have died. 'tk cloud status' could reconcile a non-terminal row against the Workflow instance API before displaying it, so a dead supervisor shows as dead rather than as running. That is the same lesson 2xm produced, applied to the read path instead of the write path.
acceptance_criteria: No run sits in a non-terminal state when its Workflow instance is absent or errored; tk cloud status shows a dead supervisor as dead. Existing stuck rows are drained.
